patterns.usage_note: が names the subject as new or newsworthy information, so it is what you use when the whole sentence is the news (雨が降ってきた) or when the subject itself is the answer to a question; は instead makes the subject a known topic and puts the news after it. Within its class, が is the default: の substitutes for it only inside a clause modifying a noun, and に, usually as には (colloquially にゃ), marks the experiencer subject of ability and understanding predicates.

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の家[いえ]から焼[や]きたてのパンの匂[にお]いがする。
examples.english: The smell of fresh-baked bread is drifting over from next door.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]がピアノのコンクールで優勝[ゆうしょう]した。
examples.english: My little sister won the piano competition.

examples.ruby: 教室[きょうしつ]の電気[でんき]がまだ消[き]えていない。
examples.english: The lights in the classroom still aren't off.

glosses: (marks the subject inside a modifying clause)
= が inside any noun-modifying or nominalized clause
patterns.usage_note: This の is が in disguise: it may mark a subject only inside a clause that modifies a noun (父の作った料理 = 父が作った料理), never in a main clause. It ties the clause more tightly to the noun and sounds a touch more literary or set-phrase-like, which is why it survives in fixed expressions such as 目の覚めるような. It is blocked when the modifying clause carries its own を-object, and speakers typically avoid it when the clause is long or already contains another の.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]の作[つく]った味噌汁[みそしる]は少[すこ]し塩辛[しおから]い。
examples.english: The miso soup my father made is a little on the salty side.

examples.ruby: 日[ひ]の暮[く]れるのが日[ひ]に日[ひ]に早[はや]くなる。
examples.english: The sun is going down a little earlier with each passing day.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]の担当[たんとう]する授業[じゅぎょう]はいつも満員[まんいん]だ。
examples.english: The classes that professor teaches are always packed.

glosses: for; as far as … is concerned
(marks the one who can or knows)
patterns.usage_note: Colloquial contraction of には marking the person a capacity, judgment or burden rests with: 俺にゃ分からない is 俺には分からない, the experiencer subject that pairs with potential, understanding and 無理/大変-type predicates. Because は is baked in it readily picks up contrast — someone else might manage it — though in many uses it simply sets the person up as the topic. Do not confuse it with the identically pronounced goal-marking にゃ, which points at a destination rather than at the one doing the knowing.

examples.ruby: 俺[おれ]にゃそんな難[むずか]しい話[はなし]は分[わ]からない。
examples.english: That kind of complicated talk is over my head.

examples.ruby: 六歳[ろくさい]の弟[おとうと]にゃ、この自転車[じてんしゃ]は大[おお]きすぎる。
examples.english: This bike is too big for my six-year-old brother.

examples.ruby: 素人[しろうと]にゃこの機械[きかい]の修理[しゅうり]は無理[むり]だ。
examples.english: Fixing this machine is beyond an amateur.
